Definition: from G1537 and G71; to lead forth:--bring forth (out), fetch (lead) out.
BiblicalUsage: exágō is a plain word for bring forth (out), fetch (lead) out. In Mark 15:20, the text says "and led him out to crucify him." In Luke 24:50, the text says "And he led them out as far as to Bethany."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that exágō matters because God really does deliver; escape is not luck, it is His hand at work. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: The Crucifixion; The Resurrection; The Ascension
